analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and extends the `stop` row in the request-parameter table (line ~2122). The new text says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-sequence matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`), and that the native block engine matches the whole output. The supplied units are base-side text for lines 3231-4000, which the patch does not touch, so I examined them as surrounding context only. No source code, wire protocol, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage behavior changes. I checked the prefix-cache threat T-041 and the TB-002/TB-007 boundaries: nothing in this change touches the SSD tier, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, or account-scoped cacheSalt. The stop-scope documentation is a functional-correctness description. I found no concrete security regression or invalidated threat assumption. One residual item: I could not verify that `ReasoningStopScope` and `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift` exist or behave as documented, because the implementation is not in the supplied evidence. Stop-sequence handling that does not match the docs could affect output correctness. That risk is not security-material under the current threat model, so I am not requesting deeper review.
